## M186: pulsing dots keep their colour; the last repainting pings (14 Nov 2026)

- **`animate-pulse` was broken everywhere.** An unlayered rule from the early look
  (`.animate-pulse { background: linear-gradient(…); animation: shimmer }`, for loading placeholders)
  beat Tailwind's utilities, so everything that pulses lost its own background: the red "recording"
  dots (message box, calls, voice feedback), amber "reconnecting" (docs, sheets, slides, boards), green
  "live" dots, the landing's text caret, about 20 places. They showed a grey shimmer, which also moved
  `background-position` every frame (a repaint, §8). The rule is gone: Tailwind's opacity pulse, in the
  element's own colour (checked in the browser: `rgb(255, 59, 48)`, animation `pulse`). The five
  loading placeholders that relied on it use `.skeleton`. **Rule:** never restyle a Tailwind utility
  class globally; placeholders are `.skeleton`.
- **The passport's step marker** (`.pp-node`, `/t/<code>`): its ping was an animated `box-shadow`; now a
  `::after` ring on `dot-ring` (transform and opacity), as M92 did for `.live-dot` and `.deck-ping`.
  The dead box-shadow rules those two still carried are removed.
- **Buttons, checked and left:** 1,476 uses of the shared `.btn-*` classes (press spring, `aria-busy`
  spinner, focus ring, sizes); the ~135 solid-colour controls that don't use them are chosen-state
  chips and tabs, not buttons. Converting them would change how tabs look for no gain.
- **Left** (loops that still repaint, each in one rare place): `flow-on` / `bento-step` (the landing's
  flow card), `play-lightning` (Quiz Clash's lightning round), `holo`, `ink-drift`, `play-static`.
- **Tested:** `/t/demo` at 390 (the marker's own animation none, ring `dot-ring`, no errors); `pnpm check`.

## M182: Messages, connections (the owner, 14 Nov)

- **Where:** Messages → Connections (mail and chat; `?space=connections`) and Settings → Connected accounts
  (everything; Google Classroom for teachers and admins). `ConnectionsPanel.tsx`.
- **Services** (`src/server/connections.ts` `SERVICES`): Gmail, Outlook, Slack (read only: the newest 20
  mails, the last message of 10 Slack direct chats, read live with the person's token, never stored),
  plus the calendars and Classroom (M200). Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord and LinkedIn can't be connected by a
  person (`ELSEWHERE` says why on the tab).
- **Off until the owner sets them up [owner]:** SESSION_SECRET (32+ characters, already needed) and, per
  maker, an app registered there with its keys in Cloudflare: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`
  (Google Cloud; Gmail's read scope is "restricted": up to 100 test users before Google's verification, and
  the full review costs money), `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID` / `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` (Azure app registration,
  free), `SLACK_CLIENT_ID` / `SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET` (a Slack app, user scopes im:read, im:history,
  users:read). Each app's sign-in return address: `https://<the site>/api/connections/callback`.
- **Security:** `POST …/start` (signed in) seals a state (who, which service, a nonce, the PKCE verifier,
  the time, a return page from a short allowed list) and sets an HttpOnly cookie with the nonce; the open
  callback accepts only a sealed state, within ten minutes, from the browser holding that cookie (so no one
  can attach their account to someone else's, or the reverse), and Google and Microsoft check PKCE. Tokens
  are sealed (`secret-box.ts`, their own context), never sent to a browser, refreshed when they run out,
  revoked on Disconnect where the service allows it. Table `oauth_connections` (0217). Unit tests
  (`connections.test.ts`: a forged state, another browser, an outside return page).
- **Tested:** the tabs at 1280 and 390, light and dark: every service shows "Not set up on UniVerse yet",
  axe clean. A real sign-in can only be tried once the owner adds the keys.

## M203 (committed as "M186"): Apps on the website (the owner, 15 Nov: "when i want to show only one app then it should switch to that one app … no other apps should be there just that one and it should be syched properly")

- **Where:** owner console → Server → **Apps on the website** (`AppsCard` in `console/server.tsx`): a switch
  per app, "Show only this app" on each, "Show every app". Saved with the other server settings
  (`POST /owner/server { apps }`, at least one; every app is stored as null so a new app shows), logged
  in Changes & undo (the raw stored value, so undo puts it back exactly). Database update **0220**
  (`server_control.apps`, a JSON list).
- **How every page follows it, without a flash:** the Worker reads the list with the server switch (once a
  minute, `cloudflare/usage-guard.ts`) and writes `<script>window.__uvApps=[…]</script>` first in every
  page's head (`withNotice(res, notice, pageApps())`); the root head script (`appHeadScript`, tested)
  then picks a shown app for `html[data-app]` and adds a style that hides every `[data-uv-app="<hidden>"]`
  and, with one app, every `[data-uv-many]` (things that only make sense with several apps). In the app,
  `src/lib/shown-apps.ts` (`useShownApps`, `shownIds`, `onlyApp`, `shownOr`, `setShownApps`) keeps the
  list (device copy `uv-apps`, checked once a visit at the public `GET /api/core/site/apps`); the pure
  part the server uses is `src/lib/shown-apps-list.ts` (**trap:** the server can't import a file with
  React hooks: keep server imports on the `-list` file).
- **What follows it:** app tabs (website, sign-in, sign-up: none with one app), the landing's planet and
  app grid (only the shown apps, hidden with one), the side menu (no "All apps" with one app, the
  switcher lists only shown apps and doesn't open with one), the hub (only shown apps; with one it sends
  people into that app), the Impact Wallet, Messages (All apps only across shown apps; no switch with
  one), the chosen and current app (`chosen-app.ts`, `current-app.ts`), where people land after signing
  in (`homeFor`), and `ShownAppsGuard` in the dashboard layout: a hidden app's page sends people to the
  first shown app's start. **Left on purpose:** public links printed or shared out in the world keep
  working (a product's `/t/<code>`, `/b/<slug>`, an aid box's `/aid/<code>`), and the owner console's
  own numbers still cover every app. It's what the website shows, not who may use what (APIs still answer).
- **Rule for new code:** anything that lists apps uses `useShownApps()`; put `data-uv-app={id}` on each
  app's item and `data-uv-many` on parts that only make sense with several apps, so they're hidden before
  the page is drawn.
- **Checked:** `shown-apps-ui.mjs` (one app and two apps, phone and computer, light and dark; axe clean),
  `apps.test.ts`, `shown-apps.test.ts`, `usage-guard.test.ts` (the Worker's list and the head script),
  `route-gates.test.ts` (the open route listed with its reason), `pnpm check`.

  `travel_cache`. The guide's **Know before you go** now says "Your passport: No visa needed (up to 90
  days)" with the source and "check the official rules before you book".
- **Traps:** NASA POWER's `T2M_MAX` climatology is the month's hottest hour, not a typical day (Bruges

  its dates and a days stepper, up/down, remove, **Shortest order** (the first city stays; nearest next,
  then reversing stretches while that shortens it); between two cities the distance, the likely way and
  time, and links (`betweenLinks()` in `travel-book.ts`: Rome2Rio every way, Google Flights over 250 km,
  Omio's search in Europe, 12Go's route page in Asia, Direct Ferries where islands are involved).
- **Day by day** (per city): "Not planned yet" and a column per day with its date and the day's total
  (amber past 9 h). Each place: kind, price, opening hours, the time to spend (by kind and name: museum
  2 h, viewpoint 30 min…; changeable), the walk or ride from the place before it, a **Move to** menu,
  earlier/later arrows and its map. **Drag** a place between days or within one (HTML5 drag and drop,
  `data-no-arrange` on the board; cards slide with `morph(…, { deep: true })`). **Plan my days** spreads the
  places by closeness (a sweep round the middle, cut into days of at least five hours, each in walking
  order). **Add places**: the ones saved in that city, or any the guide lists by kind.
- **Budget:** stays + food + getting around (each country's price level and the style, from M205),
  between cities (by distance, flights past 700 km), tickets (the guides' listed prices, read in their
  own currency: `readPrice()`; places without one counted), for all travellers, with per person. A
  sleep place's own price replaces the estimate. Says what it leaves out (getting there from home).

- **Server** (`src/server/travel-trips.ts`, routes `travel/trips…`): only members see or change a trip (a
  stranger gets "not one of yours"); limits 50 trips a person, 12 cities, 60 days, 300 places, 12 people;

## M209: Travel, the map, real places and UniVerse's own reviews (the owner, 16 Nov)

- **The ask:** "real data of places and reviews of people from that places and make the map detailed with
  all the information like the apple maps … something different that nobody has … ultra smooth". The owner
  chose (asked first): build it despite the launch pause, and reviews from UniVerse's own people (not a paid
  service).
- **Where:** Explore's third view **Map** (`/travel?view=map`, `&at=lat,lon,zoom` or `&d=<guide title>`), and
  "See on the map" on every guide. `src/components/travel/map/`: `TravelMap.tsx` (loaded only when opened,
  with MapLibre), `map-layers.ts`, `PlaceCard.tsx`, `Reviews.tsx`, `TripPicker.tsx`.
- **The map:** MapLibre GL 6.16 (BSD; `pnpm add maplibre-gl@6.16.0`) drawing **OpenFreeMap**'s vector tiles
  of OpenStreetMap (free, no account or key; its "liberty" style in light mode, "dark" in dark mode, where
  UniVerse adds the 3D buildings and the place names the dark style lacks). Tiles go straight from
  OpenFreeMap to the browser: **no Worker CPU**. MapLibre's worker is copied to `public/maplibre` by
  `scripts/copy-maplibre-assets.mjs` (dev and build, like pdf.js; gitignored) and set with `setWorkerUrl`;
  the security headers allow `tiles.openfreemap.org` (connect and img). Credits always shown in the panel.
- **What it does:** kinds of place (Sights, Food, Cafés, Drinks, Museums, Parks, Shops, Hotels, Transport;
  the tiles' `poi` classes, `src/lib/travel-map.ts`) shown in the accent with a list of those in view (one of
  each name, the notable and near first); **tap any place**: its real facts from OpenStreetMap through
  Nominatim (the tile's feature id is the OSM id ×10 + type: `osmKey`), open or closed **at the hour chosen,
  in the place's own time zone** (`src/lib/opening-hours.ts` reads the common opening_hours forms and says
  only the written hours for the rest; `src/lib/travel-local.ts`: the zone from `travel-zones.json`, made by
  `gen-travel-data.mts --zones` from the tz list), address, call, website, menu, access, payments, its photo
  and a line from Wikidata and Wikipedia; Directions (OpenStreetMap, on foot), Save, **Add to a trip** (into
  the trip's nearest city, or a new trip). **The hour slider** (the next 24 hours) lights the 3D buildings
  from where the sun really is there (`sunPosition`, `setLight`: warm low sun, a soft blue night) and shows
  sunrise, golden hour and sunset. **Layers:** 3D, photos people took nearby (Wikimedia Commons, each with its
  author and licence), stories (Wikipedia's articles about places nearby, amber pins), UniVerse reviews
  (green pins with the average). **Walk from here** (1–4 hours): the notable sights within reach strung
  nearest-next, with a look's time (an artwork 10 min, a church 20, a museum 75), drawn as a dashed line with
  numbers, arrival times in their time, and all of it into a trip in one go.
- **Reviews** (`src/server/travel-reviews.ts`, database update **0223**: `travel_reviews`,
  `travel_review_reports`): stars, words, "I live here"; one a person a place (changing it clears old
  reports); 30 a day; three reports hide one; shown by first name only; the place card shows **Locals say**
  apart from **Visitors say** and tabs for each. A place is its OSM id or `wp:<Wikipedia title>`.
- **Server** (`src/server/travel-places.ts`, routes `travel/place|where|photos|stories`): every answer kept
  in `travel_cache` (places and positions 30–90 days, photos and stories 7) and only an OSM id or a rounded
  position is sent; a busy source leaves its layer empty instead of failing.
- **Traps:** MapLibre's stylesheet makes its container `position: relative` (the map came out 300 px tall):
  the container's position is inline. A filter that matches nothing must be an expression
  (`['==', ['get','class'], '__none__']`), not `['==', 1, 0]`. OpenMapTiles files artworks as `art_gallery`
  (a museum's 75 minutes): `walkStay` checks the subclass. The map's listeners use `useEffectEvent` (React
  19.2) so the map is made once without stale state or lint-disable comments. Wikimedia rate-limits busy
  shared addresses (this machine after the data runs): photos and stories were tested on saved samples.
- **Checked:** `travel-map-ui.mjs` (the map draws in 3D; 40 sights in view; a place's facts with "Open
  until …"; a review as a local counted under Locals and deleted; Food lists restaurants; a 5-stop walk; the
  hour slider; phone panel; axe clean at 1280 dark and 390 light, the map canvas aside; no errors),
  `travel-local.test.ts`, `travel-place.test.ts`, `travel-map.test.ts`, `travel-reviews.test.ts`, `pnpm check`.

## M211: the main pages' lag, and the error log (the owner, 16 Nov)

- **The ask:** "the website and app lagg alot in the main page so please fix it and check if any errors are
  there in the system".
- **Measured** with `scripts/checks/main-pages-smooth.mjs` (new; on `local:serve`): the landing signed out
  and the hub, UniVersity's home, Travel and Trace signed in, at 390 × 844 with the CPU slowed 4× and at
  1440 × 900: long tasks while loading, frames over 3 s still and while scrolling, and a CPU profile.
  **Trap:** starting the CPU profiler stalls a slowed page for ~0.6 s; the script measures stillness before
  it starts.
- **The big one, `src/lib/scroll-motion.ts` `arrive`** (M130, content replacing a placeholder gliding in):
  it ran inside every MutationObserver callback, building its list by copying (quadratic: thousands of nodes
  when a page renders) and reading layout in the middle of React's commit: 0.3–0.5 s of each main page's
  start on a slow phone. Now: records under `[data-no-motion]` are dropped first (cached per node, `quiet`),
  a batch over 300 changes (a whole page building: its entrance moves it) is skipped, the rest is looked at
  in the next animation frame, the list is pushed not copied, `moving()` looks six levels up, and nested
  queued roots are scanned once. `PendingPage` had its own watcher doing the same job (both ran): removed;
  `arrive`'s placeholder list now includes `[role="status"][aria-label="Loading"]`.
- **The landing:** the hero scenes, the typewriter line and the rotating "hello" carry `data-no-motion`
  (they animate themselves many times a second); pointing at the app tabs builds only that app's sections
  ahead (it built all five, hidden: a half-second freeze) and loads only its code; the top bar's "scrolled"
  look comes from an IntersectionObserver on a 1 px mark (it ran on every scroll event); the product
  window's tilt is a CSS scroll timeline (`.window-tilt`; it was framer-motion's `useScroll` on the page's
  thread); counting numbers reuse one `Intl.NumberFormat` (`bits.tsx`), as `fmt()` now does
  (`src/lib/instruments.ts`: 76 ms of the hub's start).
- **Result** (phone, CPU ×4): the motion layer's share fell from 0.26–0.49 s to under 0.1 s per page; every
  main page now holds 60 frames a second while still; scrolling the landing has no long task from the page's
  code (what's left in the headless check is drawing on software graphics). The page entrance's one
  layout read (`page-transition.ts`) stays: the browser lays the page out once anyway.
- **Errors:** the live `error_reports` (production D1, read only) have nothing new since 10 Nov (a stray
  multipart POST to `/`, already refused since M159) and 7 Nov (a styling and chunk mismatch during a
  deploy); the open ones last happened 29–31 Oct and haven't come back since the fixes after them.
- **Found out of date (not changed by this):** `landing-story-ui.mjs` (looks for `#story`'s "Apps" list,
  gone since M164), `landing-pause-ui.mjs` (expects the phone hero to move at the top) and
  `landing-try-ui.mjs` (a demo it scrolls to is hidden): they fail the same way without these changes.
- **Checked:** `main-pages-smooth.mjs` before and after, `pnpm check`.

## M215: a trip's Money and Packing (16 Nov)

The owner: "add more big features in the travel app which are unique and different from others or combine
different apps features into one app". A trip (`/travel/trip?id=…`) now has three parts (`?part=`): Plan (as
before), **Money** and **Packing**, for everyone planning it, live (database update 0224).

- **Money** (`trip-money.tsx`): shared costs (what, how much, currency, kind, who paid, for whom, the day);
  where it stands (spent so far, against the Plan tab's estimate, your balance); **Settle up**, the fewest
  payments that make everyone square, each with "Mark as paid" (a payment back is a cost of kind `settle`);
  a **converter** between any of the app's currencies (World Bank yearly average rates: no outside call); and
  **what things cost there** (a coffee, lunch, dinner, a beer, a ride, a museum) per country of the trip, in
  the trip's currency and the local one, from the country's price level (said so). Sums in
  `src/lib/travel-split.ts` (cents; per currency: a bill in yen is settled in yen; an even split's leftover
  cents go to the first people so balances always add up to nothing; `readAmount` takes "12,50", "1.234,56").

## M221: the landing's crash fixed; the top bar's entries dragged into order; no names twice (16 Nov)

The owner sent the "1 problem(s) need a look" email and asked for M219's two left-outs.

- **The crash** (`error_reports`, `/`, Safari: "null is not an object (evaluating 'e.stateNode._retryCache')"): the
  landing builds an app's sections ahead, hidden in React's `Activity`, once the visitor points at its tab (M137,
  one app at a time since M211). Those sections are `next/dynamic` with no `loading`, so they have no Suspense
  boundary of their own (next's `loadable.js`): the hidden Activity caught their download. Pointing at another tab
  before it ended dropped that Activity, and when the file arrived React's `resolveRetryWakeable` read
  `stateNode._retryCache` of the dropped one (null; only its Activity case lacks the null check). Each app's part
  is now `AppPart` in `src/app/page.tsx`: the Activity with a `Suspense fallback={null}` inside, which catches the
  download and is dropped safely. **Rule:** anything shown or built inside an `Activity` that can suspend (a
  `dynamic()` without `loading`, `use()`, `lazy`) needs a Suspense boundary inside the Activity.
  `scripts/checks/landing-switch-ui.mjs` holds every download back 2.5 s and points at five tabs in a row: 16 such
  errors before, none after.
- **Dragging in the top bar:** press an entry and move sideways; the others slide aside and it drops where you let
  go (a click that ends a drag doesn't open it; right-to-left mirrored). The order is the side menu's own (the vault's
  `/~menu/<scope>`, the side menu's `data-arrange-scope`), so the installed app's side menu shows it too and More takes
  the last ones in that order. ArrangeMode now puts `menu(scope)` / `setMenu(scope, layout)` and a `rev` that grows
  with every change into `useArrange`; the side menu's entries carry `data-arrange-key` (their label), the name the bar
  uses (shortcuts: "Shortcut …"). The account menu has "Put the menu back in order" once it has been changed. Entries
  under More can't be dragged (drag one in the bar past where you want it instead, or widen the window).
- **No names twice:** on the pages of Trace, Green, Relief and Travel (`ROWED`: each has its own row of sections), the
  bar leaves out that app's entries (`APP_NAV`), which the row shows; on shared pages (Messages, Settings…) it keeps
  them, the way back. A drag there only reorders what it shows (`reorderWithin` in `src/lib/arrange.ts`).
- **Checked:** `landing-switch-ui.mjs` (above), `top-nav-ui.mjs` (no name in both the bar and the page's row; a drag
  kept after a reload and put back), the unit test of `reorderWithin`, `pnpm check`.

## M222: the notifications panel, Apple style (16 Nov)

The owner, with a picture of the old panel (navy, emoji icons): "the notification panel doesn't look good so please
work on it and make it look good and redesign it like apple style and make it ultra smooth".

- **`src/components/notifications/NotificationsPanel.tsx`** (the page bar, `Topbar`, keeps the data, the unread count
  and marking read; the panel loads on its own, fetched while the page is idle so the first tap opens it at once). iOS's
  Notification Centre in the project's look, solid surfaces (no glass, §8): grouped grey (#f2f2f7) with white cards in
  light mode, near-black (#0c0c0e) with #1c1c1e cards in dark; on a computer it floats 8 px from the window's edges,
  rounded 26 px; on a phone it fills the screen.
- **A notification:** an icon like an app's (its kind in iOS's own colours, `KIND`: messages blue, calls green, events
  red, grades indigo, announcements orange, warnings amber; a kind that is an app's id, or a link into an app, shows
  that app's icon; otherwise a grey bell), its title on two lines at most with the time ("now", "5m ago", "3h ago",
  "2d ago", then the date), a dot while unread, two lines of text, "Important" on warnings and errors. Grouped Today,
  Yesterday, Earlier; the same notification several times in a row (same title and kind) is one **stack** with layers
  under it ("2 more"): a tap opens it, "Show less" closes it. `src/lib/notification-stacks.ts` (`when`, `byDay`,
  `stacks`, tested).
- **Controls:** "Read all" and a round close button in the header; iOS's segmented control (a grey track, a white thumb,
  #636366 in dark: the `.notif-sheet` rules at the end of `globals.css`, the pills stay everywhere else) for All, Unread,
  Important; a finger swipes a card to mark it read (`SwipeRow`; a stack: all of it); Escape and the dimmed page close
  it, and focus goes back to the bell. Email notifications and "See all notifications" are one grouped card at the foot.
- **Motion:** the sheet slides in on the smooth spring as one `transform` (the compositor runs it) and out in 240 ms;
  the rows rise in one after another while it opens (`data-entering`, 35 ms apart, the glide spring); a filter or a
  stack slides the rows that stay (`morph`, deep). Reduce Motion: fades.
- **Checked:** `scripts/checks/notifications-panel-ui.mjs` (1280 dark and light, 390: no frame over 50 ms while it
  opens, the day groups, 15 notifications as 7 rows with 5 stacks, a stack opened and closed, Unread, Escape, axe),
  `pnpm check`.

## M225: the lag, measured and cut (16 Nov)

The owner: "still the website laggs alot so please fix it properly this time remember that cpu limit should not get high".
All of it in the browser (no Worker CPU). Measured on the built site with the CPU slowed 4x
(`scripts/checks/lag-profile.mjs`: loading, scrolling with the mouse moving; and traces of the page left alone):

- **What was busy:** the app's scene behind every page, on its background thread, redrew every frame the screen gives
  (up to 120 a second) at up to 2.5x sharpness: 0.35–1 s of every 5 s of one core with nobody touching anything
  (Green's the most). The landing's main thread stayed busy too (its demos, framer's `layout` on the planet's list of
  apps measuring every frame), and two `html:has(…)` rules (`.mkt-smooth`, `main#main`) restyled the root on every
  change anywhere (316 times in a scroll). Green's map breathed its dots, redrawing the whole map on the page's
  thread every frame it showed.
- **Now:** the scene draws 30 a second at 1.5x and 2 M pixels at most (`backdropLoop`, `resize` in `src/lib/backdrop.ts`):
  half the cost (Green 998 → 509 ms in 5 s, homes 349 → 167). After 30 s with no pointer, key, wheel, touch or scroll
  (`src/lib/use-idle.ts`: `useIdle`, `onIdleChange`) the scene rests and the landing's looping demos (`Live`) stop; any
  input wakes them: the landing left alone goes to 0. The `:has` rules are classes set by the page (`html.mkt-smooth-root`
  by the landing, `html.in-app` by `DashboardShell` before its first paint). The planet's list is plain `li`s; the
  landing's bars and gauges grow with transforms (`Proof`, `Glue`), not heights and widths. Green's map dots are still
  (`live={false}`: it draws when moved). Scrolling the landing: slow frames 5 → 2, long tasks 54 ms → none; the student
  home's loading long tasks 1.46 s → 0.88 s.
- **Rules:** decorative motion that loops rests when the person leaves the page alone (`useIdle`); no `:has()` on `html`
  or `body` (a class set by the page instead); a canvas on the page's thread is not `live` for decoration.

- **Timeline is a Gantt chart** (`TimelineView` in `src/components/tasks/TaskViews.tsx`): bars at their true length from
  the start (or when the card was made) to the due day, the name beside each bar (before it near the chart's end),
  milestones as diamonds, a line from each card to the cards waiting on it ("Waiting on", B9.9), rose when the waiting
  card starts before the other is due. Drag a bar to move both dates, its end edge to change the due day, or Shift+arrows
  on a focused bar to move it a day. The parent passes `onDates` (a PATCH of `startAt`/`dueAt`, optimistic).
- **Card sheet:** Starts / Due (Milestone day), the Milestone tick (it clears the start), and **Time spent**
  (`src/components/tasks/TimeLog.tsx`): a start/stop timer kept in `localStorage` `uv-task-timer:<card>` (it runs on while
  the card is closed; Stop logs it, at least a minute), time added by hand (`parseMinutes`: "1:30", "45m", "2h", "1.5"),
  entries with who and a note, the total against the estimate (rose past it). Cards show spent/estimate hours.
- **Server** (`src/server/tasks.ts`): `updateTask` takes `startAt` (refused after the due day) and `milestone`;
  `getBoard` adds `minutes` per card (one `groupBy`); `listTime` / `addTime` (1 min to 24 h, up to 500 a card, editors
  only) / `deleteTime` (your own; the board's managers anyone's); routes `/api/tasks/items/[tid]/time`,
  `/api/tasks/time/[id]`; a sample answer in `router.ts`.
- **Checked:** `scripts/checks/gantt-ui.mjs` (bars, the line, the diamond, a drag of two days saved to both dates, a start
  after the due day and a zero-minute entry refused, 1:30 logged against 2 h, the timer; axe clean at 1280 and 390, light
  and dark, no sideways scroll), the unit test in `task-calendar.test.ts`, `pnpm check`.
- **Rule:** a Gantt bar's dates change only through `onDates`; a card with no due day isn't on the timeline.

## M231: a sweep for errors, bugs and smoothness (16 Nov)

The owner: "check if any errors or bugs… make sure everything is ultra smooth", then "every button, transition, glide
or animation… like Apple", "don't let the CPU go up" and "let the other agents know". Everything below runs in the
browser: no Worker CPU added. The rules are in AGENTS.md §8 ("No double animations…") and `src/lib/motion-rules.test.ts`.

- **Live errors** (`error_reports`): a Nominatim timeout on `/api/core/travel/place` was a 500: `fetchJson`
  (`src/server/travel.ts`) now answers a slow or unreachable source with 503 "busy", like one that answers an error.
  The menu's initials (`Sidebar`, `TopNav`) no longer throw on a saved account without a name. The crawl's other
  finds were by design (the demo admin is read-only: its "tour seen" save is refused).
- **Progress bars** (about 75): `<Fill value={0..1} />` (`src/components/ui/Fill.tsx`, `.fill` in globals.css) is the
  track's full width and slides (transform, `@starting-style` for its arrival, `quick` for uploads, timers, loading).
  Many bars grew their width with framer-motion *and* were scaled by the motion layer: two animations, one re-laying
  out the page every frame. The page-loading bar (`NavProgress`), the status viewer's bars, tuner and BMI needles
  slide too. Left: stacked bars whose parts share a row (Trace market cells, consent tallies, class pulse, SVG charts)
  and the welcome tour's spotlight.
- **Loops**: framer-motion's `repeat: Infinity` ran on the page's thread every frame; now CSS (`scan-sweep`,
  `scene-tilt`, `scene-pan`, `ring-wiggle`, `slow-turn`, `twinkle`, `ring-ride`, `holo-pan`), paused while scrolling
  and with Reduce Motion. Keyframes that repainted every frame now move or fade only: the landing headline's words
  (no blur), Bento's steps, Quiz Clash's lightning glow, Night Shift's static, Skyline's rewind lines, the label shine.
- **Presses**: 39 buttons had framer's `whileTap` on top of the global press (two shrinks): now `active:scale-[…]`.
- **Page changes**: the motion layer's `arrive` (`src/lib/scroll-motion.ts`) read `window.innerHeight` on every
  frame of every count-up (a forced layout each time) and looked through the old and new page on every page change
  (55 ms of script, on a computer too). It stops early when nothing was added, and skips a page that just came in
  (`pageJustEntered()`, `page-transition.ts`: the page's entrance moves it).
- **Glass**: the full-screen dimmers behind sheets and dialogs (75) dim only, as iOS does (the moving scene behind
  was blurred again every frame); nine sticky bars with glass are solid (bars are solid, §8). The blog's "Read" link
  moves its arrow instead of widening its gap on hover.
- **Measured** (the built site, a phone with the CPU slowed 4×, `scripts/smoothness.mjs`, `main-pages-smooth.mjs`):
  scrolling and sheets were already at 0–1 slow frames and stay so; the landing's slow frames while scrolling went
  3 → 0; tab changes keep 2–3 slow frames at 4× (the new page being drawn). Checked as already right: sheets (0.46 s
  in, faster out), the loading shimmer (transform), the theme's circle reveal, hover only with a mouse, images sized.
- **Not done, on purpose:** framer `layout` on 57 list rows (rows glide when one is added; framer batches the reads);
  height animation for opening sections; the side menu's fold (installed app) still animates its width.
- **Next.js advisory** (published 16 Nov, moderate: `'use cache'` through `unstable_cache()`, which UniVerse doesn't
  use): 16.4.5 fixes it; by the two-week rule, upgrade Next and the adapter together from 30 Nov. Next stops a build
  run by an AI agent to show this notice (`next/dist/lib/upgrade/nudge.js`: only when it detects an agent, never on
  Cloudflare's builder or in CI); running the same build again at once goes through. Don't run its `next upgrade
  --agent=…` command: upgrades follow the two-week rule, Next and the Cloudflare adapter together (M77). Seven other advisories are in test and lint tools only (vitest,
  tinypool, zod in eslint's plugin): nothing in the live site.
- **Rule:** no animation on what the motion layer animates; bars `<Fill>`; loops CSS on transform / opacity; one press
  per button; no glass over the moving scene.

## M232: sharp photos in Travel, and 70 more places (16 Nov)

(Built as M228 on `claude/great-hamilton-8g8xdm` while another session used M228–M231; renumbered M232 when
merged, with that branch's map work M229 → M233. Their commits keep the old numbers.)

The owner, with a screenshot of Explore: "can you add high quality pictures here because this is look bad and also do
this for other area also if you could"; then "please add more destinations in there".

- **Why it looked bad:** the cards showed each guide's Wikivoyage *banner*, a 2100×300 strip (7:1), asked at 720 px
  wide and blown up into a 2:1 card: a blurry slice.
- **A real photo per place:** `npx tsx scripts/gen-travel-data.mts --photos` stores `photo` (a Commons file) in
  `travel-places.json`: the place's Wikidata main image (P18), else its Wikipedia article's, else Wikivoyage's own page
  image, when `photoOk` (`src/lib/travel-guide.ts`) agrees: a bitmap photo, ≥1600 px wide, ratio 1.2–2.6, and no map,
  flag, locator, collage, satellite or banner in its name. `null` means looked for and none found. Every chosen photo
  was looked at on contact sheets; bad ones (maps, satellite views, dull or wrong shots) are replaced by hand with the
  **7th column** of a `travel-ideas.ts` row (`undefined` in the 6th keeps the guide's banner; `''` means no photo).
- **Trap:** from cloud machines Wikimedia's action API (`/w/api.php`) answers 429. The script uses only the REST
  endpoints (`/api/rest_v1/page/summary`, `/w/rest.php/v1/file`), `Special:EntityData`, one request at a time with a
  pause; no SPARQL, no proxies. Thumbnails only come at Wikimedia's standard widths (`PHOTO_STEPS`: 500, 960, 1280, 1920).
- **Shown sharp:** `Cover` (`travel-ui.tsx`) takes `photo`, `banner` and `sizes` and draws a plain `<img>` through
  `Photo` (`components/ui`, which now takes a `srcSet` for pictures kept elsewhere) with `commonsSrcSet`: the browser
  picks the width for the card and the screen; lazy below the fold, `fetchPriority="high"` for the first cards. If the
  photo fails it falls back to the banner, then the gradient. Explore, Find where to go, Trips, the guide and the trip
  header all use it (`CARD_SIZES`, or `100vw` for headers).
- **Any other place's guide:** `photoFor` in `src/server/travel.ts` looks up the Wikidata / Wikivoyage photo once a
  month (`photo1:` in the travel cache, 3–4 small requests on the first visit) and returns `guide.photo`; Explore's own
  places use their row's photo.
- **Other areas:** the map's place card (`PlaceCard.tsx`) showed Wikipedia story pictures fetched at 320 px and
  Commons photos at 400 px across a 24 rem card; they now come in the same widths (`commonsFileOf` finds the file
  behind a thumbnail address). Checked and left: the landing (drawn scenes, no photos), the hub, Green's proof photos
  and other uploads (shown small, or already in several widths through `Photo`), the map's round photo markers and the
  search's 40 px thumbnails.
- **70 more places** (145 → 215: e.g. Lyon, Cinque Terre, Dolomites, San Sebastián, Bergen, Faroe Islands, Nara,
  Bhutan, Wadi Rum, Namibia, Madagascar, Boston, Yellowstone, Iguazu Falls, Uyuni, Milford Sound). `--places` now reads
  only places not read yet or without a climate (`--all` for everything). The Faroe Islands' price level is a guess
  (1.3, DKK) in `travel-money.json` and the script.
- **Finished after the first pass (the owner: "please work on this and whatever is left"):** all 215 places have a
  climate (NASA POWER for the 30 new ones whose guides have none; in a cloud session run the script with
  `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`, or Node's fetch can't resolve the host); Lake Como borrows Milan's guide climate
  (`CLIMATE_LIKE`: NASA's grid averaged the lake with the Alps, 2 °C January highs). Every chosen photo has now been
  looked at (Commons' REST search, `/w/rest.php/v1/search/page`, finds files when the action API won't answer);
  Tunis (Sidi Bou Said), Uyuni (the salt flat), Puerto Vallarta (its crowned church), Hokkaido (Shiretoko's lakes) and
  Hanoi (the Huc Bridge) got hand-picked photos; no place shows a banner any more.
- **Also:** a guide's header on a phone left its text running under the "← Explore" button (a long first paragraph):
  it has room at the top now (`pt-16`, as the trip's header).
- **Checked:** `scripts/checks/travel-photos-ui.mjs` (Explore, Find, Trips, the Kyoto and Ghent guides at 1280 and 390
  at 2x, light and dark: photos not banners, the width picked covers the pixels shown, cards below the fold lazy, axe,
  no sideways scroll). Cloud sessions can't load Wikimedia's pictures (429), so there run it with `STAND_IN=1`: the
  photo requests are answered with labelled stand-ins of the asked width. Unit tests for `photoOk`, `commonsFileOf`,
  `commonsSrcSet`; `pnpm check`.
## M233: Travel's map in Apple Maps' look, and walks you can follow (16 Nov)

The owner, on a walk in Travel → Map: "i cant understand the path and see the things clearly in the map please
fix it properly"; then, showing Apple Maps' directions: "make it like the 2nd photo… make the whole map design
like this for the other things also… this is not how apple map looks like so please do it properly".

- **The walk along real streets.** `routeUrl` / `routeOf` / `withLegs` (`src/lib/travel-map.ts`, tested): the
  browser asks FOSSGIS's free OSRM walking router (`routing.openstreetmap.de/routed-foot/…/driving/…`, no
  account; credited in the map's footer while a walk shows; added to `connect-src` in `security-headers.ts`)
  once per walk; its legs replace the estimated minutes and km. Without an answer the walk stays straight and
  dashed, and the card says so. A walk keeps its `start` (it used to follow the map's middle when dragged).
- **The walk's look** (`map-layers.ts`): one blue line with a darker edge (`ROUTE`), a blue start dot, numbered
  blue stops with their names, the walking minutes in one bubble just above its longest stretch (`bubbleAt`;
  a stretchable `uv-bubble` image). While a walk shows, `focusWalk` fades the other pins and their names and
  hides the 3D buildings: with the hills on, buildings draw after the flat map and covered the line even
  laid flat (tried first). The view goes flat (pitch 0, north up). **Tried and dropped:** arrows along the
  line (they read as breaks) and a bubble per stretch (crowded on phones).
- **The walk's card:** Apple's header (round Share, the walk with a blue summary pill, round close "End walk");
  Share uses the phone's share sheet or copies the walk's Google Maps link; "Directions in Google Maps"
  (`walkInGoogle`, up to nine stops between start and end).
- **The map design** (`src/components/travel/map/map-style.ts`): Travel's own style in place of OpenFreeMap's
  liberty and dark, on the same tiles (`tiles.openfreemap.org/planet`, OpenMapTiles schema) and fonts (Noto
  Sans Regular, Bold, Italic): cream land, green parks, blue water, white streets in light; blue-slate land,
  deep green parks, blue water, slate streets in dark (Apple Maps' tones); street names in small spaced
  capitals, district names in spaced bold capitals. No sprite: every icon is ours. `STYLE` is now the two
  style objects (so `applied` refs hold objects). The first symbol layer (street names) is Regular, which
  `fontOf` hands to our labels; `bold` swaps Regular for Bold. Green's places map and Relief's alerts map use
  the same `STYLE`, so they changed too.
- **Pins:** names beside the pin, bold, in the pin's colour (`labelColor`, lighter on the dark map). The map's
  buttons in two rounded capsules (zoom; north, where I am, layers). The 3D switch is off by default and the
  map opens flat, as Apple's does (a choice already kept on the device stays).
- **The world maps** (`WorldCanvas.tsx` `PAL`: Trace, Relief, Green, the landing, World Pin): blue sea and
  cream land in light, navy sea and slate land in dark, the same tones.
- **Checked** on a made-up neighbourhood (this machine can't reach OpenFreeMap or the router): vector tiles
  built with geojson-vt and vt-pbf in the scratchpad, served by Playwright in place of OpenFreeMap's, the
  router's real answer format imitated along the streets (and refused, for the straight fallback): computer
  and phone, light and dark, no page errors, axe clean on the walk card. **Not seen yet on the real map:**
  look at Travel → Map in a city once it is live (colours on real parks, rivers and buildings).

## M234: calls from a phone fill the screen, clearer sound, the screen stays awake (16–17 Nov)

The owner, 16 Nov: "when he join the camera doesnt cover the area it should if he joins from the phone and the audio
quality is bad… check if any other problems are there like this".

- **The picture's shape.** Every tile was a 16:9 box with `object-cover`, so a phone's tall picture was cut to a
  band of a face on a laptop. `videoFit(videoRatio, boxRatio)` (`src/lib/meet.ts`, tested) covers the box when the
  shapes are close and shows the whole picture (`contain`) when they differ by more than 1.35x; a shared screen is
  always `contain`. A tall picture (`isPortrait`) gets a tall 3:4 tile in the grid, its height capped to the window
  (checked: a phone's 360×640 picture now fills a 444×592 tile on a laptop). The Tile measures its box and the
  video (ResizeObserver, `loadedmetadata`, `resize`: a phone turned sideways changes it).
- **Two people on a phone** (`phoneDuo`): the other person fills the screen and you are a small 3:4 tile in the
  corner, as FaceTime and WhatsApp do; those tiles pass `fill` (the layout sizes them, the picture covers them).
- **Sound.** "Strong" noise removal (RNNoise plus a gate) was the default on every call: it chewed words and cut the
  starts and ends of sentences. The default is now **Standard** (the browser's own echo and noise handling);
  Strong stays a choice, with a gentler gate (open −58 dB, close −64 dB, 400 ms hold). Opus stays at 64 kbps.
- **Sweep:** a phone's screen locked during a call (camera and sound stopped): `useWakeLock`
  (`src/lib/use-wake-lock.ts`) keeps it awake while the call is live. No doubled audio found.
- **Rules:** a new kind of tile gets its fit from `videoFit` (or `fill` when the layout sizes it), never a fixed
  `object-cover`; anything holding a phone's screen during a live activity uses `useWakeLock`.

  middle) and to, swap, Walk / Cycle / Drive (FOSSGIS's foot, bike and car routers, from the browser), up to three

- **Where:** the trip page's **Phrases** part (`trip-phrases.tsx`, loaded with `next/dynamic` only when opened).

## M260: live turn-by-turn navigation on Travel's map, and more Google + Apple Maps directions features (17 Nov)

The owner, 17 Nov: "do all the left over … the maps … needs to upgrade on the next level … combined features of both google
maps and apple maps … specially the directions part where it navigates you live … ultra smooth" (the owner's exception to
the launch pause).

- **Left over from M259, still left over:** this machine can't reach Wikivoyage, Wikimedia Commons or Wikidata (the
  network's gateway refuses them, 403), so the 160 new hand-picked places still have no photo, banner or climate. Nothing
  was made up. **[next session with Wikimedia access]** the same three commands as M259's note (`gen-travel-data.mts
  --places`, `--photos` checked by eye, then `gen-destinations.mts`).
- **Live navigation** (`src/components/travel/map/Navigate.tsx`; logic in `src/lib/navigation.ts`, tested): Directions →
  **Start** on the chosen route. The map goes full screen; the panel and the map's buttons step aside. The phone's position
  (`watchPosition`, high accuracy; never sent anywhere) is snapped to the route (`snapTo`: the nearest point, going back
  costs as much as being off, so a route that passes itself keeps the right part). **Smooth:** the arrow (a MapLibre
  `Marker`, flat on the map, turned with it) glides between fixes *along the route* (`pointAt`, around corners) over the
  time between fixes; the bearing (the route's direction 20 m ahead, `headingAt`) and the zoom ease every frame
  (`turnToward`, exponential); the camera is `jumpTo` on our own `requestAnimationFrame`, tilted (walk 45°, cycle 50°,
  drive 58°) with you low on the screen (`setPadding` top 42%); the loop rests when nothing moves. **No React render a
  frame:** React renders once a fix (the banner and the bar). The travelled part fades to grey by moving a `line-gradient`
  step (`navGradient`, source `uv-nav` with `lineMetrics`), not new data each frame. **Driving:** the zoom pulls out with
  speed and in before a turn (`followZoom`), three spoken cues (800, 250, 70 m) instead of two, a km/h bubble.
- **The screen:** a dark banner (both themes) with the turn's arrow (`TurnIcon.tsx`: one drawn arrow for every angle,
  U-turn, roundabout, start, stop, end), the metres counting down (`bannerDistance`) and the words, sliding in (`.swap`) when
  the turn changes; "Then …" when the next turn is within 1 km; on the right mute, the whole route (overview) and **share my
  arrival time** (share sheet or copied: "On my way to …: arriving about 14:35" with a link to the place); at the bottom the
  arrival time, minutes and distance left (router pace, `progressAt`), "See the turns" (the turns still to come), **End**.
  Moving the map yourself stops following and shows **Re-centre** (a finger or the mouse pauses the camera at once on
  `pointerdown`: a `jumpTo` every frame would cancel MapLibre's drag; a plain tap lets it carry on). **Arrival**
  (`hasArrived`: 15 m walking, 30 m driving) stops the position and shows a card: the place, time and distance travelled,
  **Look around** (Panoramax street photos there), Done (back to the directions card). The screen stays awake
  (`useWakeLock`) until arrival.
- **Spoken turns** (`cueAt`, `cueText`): each said once ("Head off along X for 550 metres, then turn right onto Y", "In 100
  metres, turn right onto Y", "Turn right onto Y", "Your destination is in 60 metres", "You have arrived at your
  destination"). The browser's own voice (`speechSynthesis`, free, nothing sent); `primeSpeech()` on the Start press (phones
  speak only after a tap). The line goes into an `aria-live` element first and is spoken **as the page shows it**: when the
  page is translated (UiTranslator) the translated words in the page's language, else English. Mute is remembered on the
  device (`uv-nav-muted`).
- **A new route when you leave it:** three fixes in a row further off than 30 m (45 driving) plus up to 30 m of the phone's
  own doubt (`isOff`) ask the same router again from where you are (through the stops not yet reached), at most once in 10
  s; "Finding a new route…", then the arrow glides onto the new line.
- **Directions, more of Google's and Apple's** (`MapTools.tsx`): **stops on the way** (up to three, orange dots; the router
  takes them in order, without other ways then); **Leave now / Leave at / Arrive by** with a time (each route says "Arrive
  14:35" or "Leave by 13:50"); **Avoid** tolls, motorways or ferries when driving (OSRM's `exclude`, one at a time as the
  car profile allows; if the router refuses, the fastest is shown and the card says so); each route's **time in a bubble on
  the map**, the others grey with **+N min** (`bubbleSpot`: on the stretch furthest from the other routes; tap one to take it)
  and the same in the list; "live traffic isn't counted" under driving times; **Home, Work and recent places** as chips under
  an empty field (kept on the device, `uv-map-kept`; set from "what's here": Set as Home / Set as Work); turn arrows in the
  list. `routesOf` now reads every leg's turns with their place, time, kind and roundabout exit; `stepText` knows ramps,
  roundabout exits, end of road and new names.
- **A real bug fixed:** on a phone, "Directions to here" left the directions in the closed bottom sheet; it opens now.
- **Checked:** `navigation.test.ts` (11), `pnpm check`; `scripts/checks/travel-nav-ui.mjs` on `local:dev` with a simulated
  walk (Playwright geolocation; router, Nominatim and tiles answered in the test): 1280 dark and 390 light, both routes with
  +4 min, Start, the countdown 560 → 170 m, the nine spoken lines, one new route after going off, Re-centre after a drag, the
  turns list, arrival, back to directions; axe clean, no sideways scroll, no page errors. **Not seen live:** real GPS on a
  phone, the real router's turns and real tiles under the route (this machine can't reach them): walk a few streets with it
  once merged.
- **Left out on purpose:** live traffic (needs a paid service), lane guidance (the free router has no lanes), speed limits,
  a live-moving shared arrival link (it would need the server to hold your position: the shared message has the time).

## M261: security updates (17 Nov)

The owner, 17 Nov: "run the next js security upgrade now and whatever else is there" (after `next dev` printed Next.js's
security notice).

- **Before:** `pnpm audit` found 8: Next.js 16.4.4 (moderate: a `'use cache'` function called through `unstable_cache()`
  could show one root param's data under another; fixed in 16.4.5), and in the tools that only run on a developer's
  machine: Vitest 3.2.4 and its `@vitest/mocker` (critical, moderate: its UI server and mock redirects could read files),
  Tinypool (critical: prototype pollution to code execution) and Zod inside eslint-plugin-react-hooks (high: memory on

## M265: a trip's ways follow the real roads, a day's walk the streets (17 Nov)

The owner, 17 Nov, on a screenshot of M264's test (the map empty because the test refused the tiles; live, the streets
show): "it shows all the directions … like take left or right then the direction line should bend like that".

- **Between cities** (`roadLegs`, `legKey`, `bow` in `map-world.ts`, tested): each way under 1,500 km that isn't flown or
  sailed (the stop's `mode`, M247) is asked of FOSSGIS's car router from the browser (`directionsUrl('car', …)`, one
  request per way, at most 12, once per trip); its path replaces the straight line (`tripFeatures(…, legs)`). Flights and
  ferries are a gentle arc (`bow`). Until (or unless) the router answers, straight lines. Trains use the road's path (no
  free rail router): close enough on a map of a country.
- **A chosen day:** its places (in their order, up to 10) are joined by the walking router's path along the streets (role
  `walk`, the directions' blue with its darker edge, `uv-trip-walk`), and the map frames that day's places (it framed the
  whole trip before, which left the walk tiny).
- **No Worker CPU:** the routers answer the browser; `routing.openstreetmap.de` was already in `connect-src` (M233).

## M234

(Built as M232 on `claude/funny-galileo-y4mz9r` while another session used M232–M233 for Travel; renumbered
M234–M236 when merged. Their commits keep the old numbers.)

**Section tabs no longer jump down** (the owner, 16 Nov: "when i switch to report cards then the section
line goes down… same happening in other also"). With the menu across the top (M219), `Topbar` drew a row
only when a page had buttons (`rightNode` / `action`), so a tab with a button (Report cards' "New round")
pushed the tabs lower than its neighbours. Now `SectionTabs` ends its row with an empty `[data-tabs-end]`
slot, and `Topbar` (top-nav mode, no `leftNode`) portals its buttons there instead of drawing its own row:
every page in a tab group keeps the tabs at the same height (checked on Insights' tabs: 78 px on four
pages). Rules: the slot is found when `Topbar` mounts, as the first `[data-tabs-end]` under `Topbar`'s
parent; a page that renders its tabs only after loading keeps the old row. Phones and the installed app
(side menu) are unchanged.

## M236

**A deep check of every page and every row of tabs** (the owner, 16 Nov: "check for more… go through sub
pages… everything is in place and works properly and the animations are properly established"). On the
built site (`local:build` + `local:serve`): every page in the guide's list (205, minus sign-in and
public-code pages) opened as student, teacher and admin at 1440 and 390 px (410 visits), recording page
errors, failed requests, error screens, empty pages, sideways scroll, layout shift, text left invisible
by an animation and animations that never end; then every row of section tabs clicked through as a
person would (298 clicks, both widths), watching the row frame by frame. Found and fixed:
- **The row of tabs vanished for ~300 ms** on tabs whose page wasn't downloaded yet (Marketplace, Offline,
  Library, Impact rooms and League, Startups, Campus map, Medical, Collaborate's Files / Code / Tasks…;
  worst on phones, which have no hover to preload). `(dashboard)/loading.tsx` now draws the page's real

  layer's `arrive` (`scroll-motion.ts`) treated the new tab row as arriving content. It now skips the

- **The loading skeleton still drew the old title bar** (titles went in M210, the top menu came in M219), so
  every slow page jumped up when it arrived: its `Title` is now only the installed app's bar.

  on top of the motion layer's own reveal: the double animation §8 forbids); removed there and in
  `SupportPanel`. Only the website (landing) keeps `whileInView`.
- **Hover-only things invisible on touch screens** (§6): Green's "Delete this action", Settings' "Change
  photo" (lighter dimming on touch), Collaborate's quick buttons and Messages' "Chat options" on tablets,
  Communities' "Join", the bar values on Finances and Impact: now `pointer-fine:opacity-0
  pointer-fine:group-hover:opacity-100` (hidden only where there's a mouse).
Checked and fine: no crashes, error screens, empty pages or sideways scroll anywhere; Trace's PRO pages
answer a student with "Start your brand first"; the logo's light plays three times by design; the demo
admin's 403 on saving a setting is its read-only design; `/api/calendar-link` 503 locally is the missing
`SESSION_SECRET` ([owner]); a one-off ChunkLoadError is handled by `recovery-script.ts`. The crawl scripts
were one-offs (not committed); `scripts/checks/main-pages-smooth.mjs` and the axe checks remain the kept ones.

## The owner's error email of 17 Nov ("2 problem(s) need a look")

- **"undefined" on /travel, iOS Safari, 5 times by 2 people** (diagnosed by the reporter as an inbox crash: wrong): the
  error monitor's capture-phase `error` listener on `window` also hears a picture, video or sound that failed to load
  (Travel's Commons photos, often on iOS Safari); such an event has no `error` and no `message`, so it was reported as
  "undefined". Nobody saw a broken page. `src/lib/error-monitor.ts` now leaves alone failed loads on any element but
  scripts and stylesheets (still reported as `ChunkLoadError`), events with nothing in them, and promises turned down
  with nothing.
- **`/api/core/travel/place` timed out once** (16 Nov 17:02): already fixed by M231 the same evening (a slow source
  answers 503 "busy", not a site error); not seen since.
- **[owner]:** mark both reports resolved in the console (Overview → Problems) once this is live.

## M285: Travel's map asks the server less while you move it (18 Nov)

The owner: "make travel app more efficient… ultra smooth specially maps". Measured on the built site (Paris, dragging and
zooming, CPU slowed 4×): almost all the work while moving is MapLibre drawing (already tuned in M259/M267: pixel ratio
capped at 2, short label fades, tiles kept). What wasted Worker requests: every stop of the map asked for UniVerse's
reviews of the new view (the box was matched to ~100 m) and the stories again at every zoom.

- `nearKey` / `boxKey` (`src/lib/travel-map.ts`, tested): the middle snapped to 0.02° (~2 km) with a radius from four
  steps, the box outwards to 0.05° (~5 km); a small pan reuses the answer (SWR's key doesn't change).
- **Rule:** what a map view asks the server for is snapped to a grid; never a key from the exact view.

## M289: nothing cut off on a phone: grids, UniVersity's pages and a crawl that finds it (18 Nov)

The owner: "please do a lot more like this and then merge it". Screenshots of UniVersity's main pages (student and
teacher), Green, Relief, Trace and the hub on a phone and a computer, then a crawl of all 213 pages.

- **The cause, found once and fixed everywhere:** a grid given columns only from a breakpoint up (`grid sm:grid-cols-2`)
  is one `auto` column on a phone, and that column grows to its longest line that won't break (a `truncate`, a
  `whitespace-nowrap`), so a card's text ran past its edge and was cut off: "Finish setting up your account" on every
  home, the empty-state cards (`FeatureGuide`) on ~15 pages, a teacher's course cards, the timetable's empty week. **422
  grids in 209 files** got `grid-cols-1` (one column that shrinks to the screen). `src/lib/layout-rules.test.ts` fails a
  new one.
- **The crawl** (`scripts/crawl.mjs --layout`) now also reports **text cut off by a box that clips** (not an ellipsis,
  not inside something that scrolls, not screen-reader text). On phones: 74 cut-off texts on 25 pages before, 1 after
  (fixed too: the admin home's long revenue figure, `KpiCard` 22 px on a phone when the figure is longer than 7
  characters). On a computer: none, no part sticking out.
- **UniVersity:** the course page's buttons (All my grades, Message instructor; Invite students, Teaching team, Copy to a
  new term, Gradebook, Quizzes) wrap instead of running off a phone; Grades: the transcript's title no longer squeezed
  to a letter by its course picker, its table fits a phone (`px-2 sm:px-4`), and rows no longer slide in twice
  (framer-motion on each row on top of the motion layer); "Finish setting up your account" is a solid card (it was glass).
  `FeatureGuide`'s Example badge 11 px (was 10).
- **Looked at and left:** the remaining "overlaps" in the crawl are buttons placed on cards on purpose (a course's colour,
  a folder's +, a tool's star), a link wrapping onto two lines, and map chips scrolled partly out of their strip; the
  read-only demo admin's `PATCH /users/me` 403 (the tour's "seen", tests only); `/api/calendar-link` 503 locally (no
  `SESSION_SECRET`).
- **Checked:** the phone and computer crawls (213 pages each, `--layout`), the Travel checks, `pnpm check`. Browser only.
- **Rules:** a grid with columns from a breakpoint up also gets `grid-cols-1`; after a layout change run
  `node scripts/crawl.mjs <url> --phone --layout` and read the "cut off" lines.

## M301: an authenticator app as everyone's second sign-in step (18 Nov)

The owner's 32 features, Platform 1. Two-step sign-in was for admins and the owner only (an emailed code, or a passkey).

- **Settings → Privacy & Security → Authenticator app** (`AuthenticatorApp` in `SignInSecurity.tsx`; `/auth/app-code`,
  `/start`, `/confirm`, `/off` in `src/server/modules/auth.ts`): a 20-byte secret shown once as a QR code (`otpauth://`)
  and as a key, sealed with `secret-box` (`users.totpSecret`, context `totp:<id>`); the first right code turns it on
  (`users.totpOn`) and returns this sign-in's pass, so the person isn't asked again at once; turning it off needs a
  current code. Five wrong codes lock for 15 minutes (`takeTry`), as the emailed codes.
- **Codes** (`src/server/totp.ts`): RFC 6238 (HMAC-SHA1, 30 s, 6 digits; tested with the RFC's own values), the step
  either side for a phone's clock, and never the same step twice (`users.totpStep`).
- **Who is asked** (`needsTwoStep(role, token, app)`): admins as before (when email works) and anyone with `totpOn`
  (needs only `SESSION_SECRET`); `TWO_STEP_OFF` still stops both. Passed through in `getSessionUser`, the router and
  the Worker's light paths (`fast-api.ts` reads `totpOn` with the caller). `TwoStepPanel` asks for the app's code
  (email only for admins); emailed codes are now refused for non-admins (they cost emails).
- 0246 (`users.totpSecret`, `totpOn`, `totpStep`). Tests: `totp.test.ts`.
- **Rule:** never send `totpSecret` anywhere after setup; "Download my data" skips it.

## M326: scrolling glides, like tripist.app (18 Nov)

The owner: "take inspiration from this website… it takes time to scroll and it feels really good". tripist.app is a
Framer site whose Smooth Scroll part runs Lenis with `duration = intensity / 10`, and it sets 25: each wheel turn moves
a target and the page eases there over 2.5 s on Lenis's expo-out curve (`1.001 − 2^(−10t)`: half the way in a quarter
of a second, then a long soft stop). No new library: **`src/lib/smooth-scroll.ts`** (about 80 lines), started with the
other motion in `ScrollMotion.tsx`, on every page (the landing and the app: both scroll the document).

- **Native everywhere else:** touch (phones keep their own momentum, as tripist), keys, the scroll bar, `#links`,
  Shift / Ctrl / Alt / ⌘ + wheel (sideways, pinch zoom), a wheel something already took (`defaultPrevented`: maps,
  games), canvases, frames, videos, fields, dialogs, `.maplibregl-map`, `data-scroll-native`, fixed bars and sheets, a
  part that scrolls by itself until its end (or always, with `overscroll-behavior: contain`), a page locked with
  `overflow: hidden` (viewers), the top and the end (the device's bounce). A key, the scroll bar or a new page moving
  the page lets the glide go (it checks `scrollY` each frame). `scrollTo({ behavior: 'instant' })`, so the landing's
  `scroll-behavior: smooth` doesn't fight it.
- **Off** with Reduce Motion (the device's or the app's) and with **Settings → Appearance → Smooth scrolling** (on by
  default; `uv-smooth` = '0' on the device; `SMOOTH_EVENT`).
- While anything scrolls (`html[data-scrolling]`), frames don't catch the wheel (`pointer-events: none` on `iframe`).
- Measured (dev server, 1280 px): one 400 px wheel turn on the landing 136 → 226 → 285 → 328 … 398 px every 150 ms;
  the student home and Travel the same; End during a glide jumps to the end. Test: `smooth-scroll.test.ts`.
- **For code that builds on it:** a part with its own wheel handling should `preventDefault` (or carry
  `data-scroll-native`); never put `scroll-behavior: smooth` on `html` for the glide's sake.

  the chosen interests (8: famous, history, museums, parks and views, food, shopping, nightlife, children), how much the
  guide says, a photo or Wikidata item, and nearness to the stay; the best ones split over the days **by direction from
  the stay** (each day one part of town; its district named in the message), each day the **shortest round** from the
  stay, then **lunch** near where you are at 12:30, a **coffee** mid-afternoon (Relaxed and Balanced), **dinner** near
  the last place when the day runs past 16:30, a **bar** after it for Nightlife. Paces: Relaxed 3 places from 10:00,
  Balanced 4 from 9:00, Packed 6 from 8:30 (`most`: the longest stay at one place). Lighter first and last days (half the
  places; the first starts at 14:00, after check-in). Places already on the trip stay; unplanned ones are fitted in.
  Closed or "temporarily" places are skipped; nothing is added twice. Test: `travel-itinerary.test.ts`.
- **On a trip:** ✨ → `TripPlanSheet` (`trip-plan.tsx`): where you're staying (typed and found with `/travel/where`,
  or one saved on a trip; kept as the city's stay), pace, interests, every day or only the empty ones, lighter first and
  last days.
- **On Trips:** "Booked a hotel? Get your days planned" → `BookedPlan`: the hotel typed (its town becomes the city), or
  the booking confirmation **pasted and read** (`POST /travel/booking/read`, `src/server/travel-booking.ts`: one AI
  request within the day's allowance and the owner's AI switch, nothing kept), or just a city; arrival date and nights →
  a new trip with the stay and every day planned, then the trip opens.
- **`POST /travel/trips/:id/plan`** (`planTravelStop`): up to 60 places a call (the page sends more in further calls),
  5 a statement, the moves of places already there (only that city's), checked like any added place.
- **When each day starts** is the city's own: `travel_trip_stops.starts` (JSON day → minutes, 5:00–15:00 on the half
  hour, `readStarts`), set by the planner and by the day's options, shared with everyone on the trip. Database update
  **0256**.
- Tried in a browser: "Hotel Avenida Palace, Lisbon", 3 nights, History and Food → four days, each in one part of town,
  with photos, times, walks, lunch and dinner.

## M332: the wheel's glide on Lenis's own clock (19 Nov)

The owner: "it goes slow for 1 sec then it goes fast then again i scroll it happens same… i need the exact scroll and
smoothness". tripist's Framer part (`SmoothScroll_Prod`) runs `new Lenis({ duration: intensity / 10 })` with intensity
25 (read from its page module): M326's curve was right. Its clock wasn't: `t = now − start` with `start` taken in the
wheel handler. Browsers hand wheel events to the page at the start of a frame, after the frame's timestamp is set, so
`now < start` and the frame moved by `glideEase(0)` ≈ 0.1%. A trackpad or a spun wheel sends an event nearly every
frame: the page stalled for the whole gesture and rushed when it ended. Headless tests miss it (their events arrive
between frames). **`src/lib/smooth-scroll.ts`** now advances `elapsed` by the time since the previous frame (a frame's
worth on the first), resets it to 0 on a turn, and rounds the target, all as Lenis's `Animate.advance` / `scrollTo`;
`glideAt(from, to, elapsed)`. Compared with the real Lenis 1.3.4 injected into the landing (our glide off): one notch,
a flick of four and a swipe match to a few pixels every 100 ms.

- **For code that builds on it:** never time a frame-driven animation from an event's `performance.now()`; step it
  with the rAF timestamps.

sending route in `COSTLY`; a fetch of a person's link uses `privateHost` and manual redirects; after editing

## M341: encrypted photos, files, videos and voice notes in private chats (19 Nov)

The owner: "encrypted message system for security of the website". Private chats (Stage 5 · B7.6, X25519 device keys,
`src/lib/e2e.ts`) were text only. Now:

- **Sending** (`ChatWindow` `send`, private branch): first `encryptForChat(…, '')` (throws if the other person has no
  device yet, so nothing is uploaded for nobody); each file (photos shrunk first) is encrypted with a fresh AES-256-GCM
  key (`encryptFile`), uploaded as `private.enc` (`application/octet-stream`, the new `.enc` in `MIME_BY_EXT`, served as
  an attachment), and the message's encrypted text is an envelope (`fileEnvelope`: a `\u0001uvfile:` mark + JSON of url,
  key, nonce, name, type, size, kind, a voice note's length and bars, the caption). Albums go as one message a photo.
  Stickers stay out of private chats.
- **Opening** (`PrivateText` → `PrivateAttachment`): `readEnvelope` accepts only this site's file addresses
  (`isUploadedFileUrl`); photos, videos and voice notes are fetched and decrypted at once into a `blob:` address (freed on
  unmount), other files on tap; AES-GCM refuses anything changed on the way. "End-to-end encrypted" under each.
- The server sees who is in the chat, when, and the scrambled bytes' size; never the key, name or type.
- **For code that builds on it:** a new kind of private content goes in the envelope, never in the message's plain
  fields; forwarding, search, translation and AI stay off in private chats.

## M342: Meet & call, who joined, My room, reactions, the security code (19 Nov)

The owner, asked which Meet & call features: "All of them and encrypted system in this also".

- **Already there, checked:** the pre-join screen (camera preview, `MicMeter`, test sound, devices, backgrounds, 2G mode)
  and meeting notes posted into the call's chat (`src/server/meeting-notes.ts` `deliver`).
- **Who joined:** `endCall` (src/server/calls.ts) adds `people` (first names, up to 8) from `call_stats` rows with time
  connected, plus the person ending it when answered; a group call's chat card says "With …".
- **My room:** `personalRoomId(userId)` = `l_` + 16 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(SESSION_SECRET, `personal-room:<id>`): the same
  call link every time, unguessable from the account id, refused without a 32+ character secret. `POST /api/calls/links
  { personal: true }`; a row under the four tiles on Meet & call opens it (`NewMeeting personal`). The room's host is its
  owner (the CallRoom's `creator`, set once).
- **Reactions:** `FloatingReactions` is CSS now (`react-rise` 3 s on transform and opacity, a sway per reaction from its
  id), bigger, with five `react-spark` copies for 👏 and 🎉; Reduce Motion only fades. The name chip is 11 px.
- **Encryption, honestly:** calls of up to six connect directly (WebRTC: DTLS-SRTP, end to end); bigger calls with the SFU
  set up go through Cloudflare Realtime (encrypted in transit, readable there). A lock in the call's bar opens a sheet:
  direct calls list each person with a **security code** (`securityCode`: SHA-256 of both SDP fingerprints in a fixed
  order, four groups of four digits, the same at both ends; a man in the middle swapping certificates changes it);
  SFU calls say so plainly. True end-to-end encryption through the SFU (insertable streams with keys from the chat's
  device keys) is **left out**: say it if the owner asks for it.
- **Phones:** the call bar's seven buttons pushed Leave off a 390 px screen: Share screen is in More on phones
  (`phoneOnly` items), the bar keeps six and Leave.
- Tested on the built site with two people (fake camera): both codes 6860 3677 2818 7511, the clap with its sparks on the
  other screen, `people` on the call's message, steady and personal room links.

## M344: Messages' gaps against the other apps: live location, spoilers, events, QR invites, read receipts (19 Nov)

The owner: "Add all features that all messaging and video call and meeting apps has… just research all the things we
need". An inventory of about 100 features (WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, iMessage, Messenger, Slack, Discord, Teams, Zoom,
Meet, FaceTime) against the code found nearly everything already in (replies, threads, reactions, editing with history,
undo send, pins, stars, polls, stickers, disappearing and view-once, voice and video notes, stories, communities and
channels, broadcasts, bots, translation, AI catch-up, folders, archive, chat lock, export, wallpapers, effects, silent send,
slow mode, roles, custom emoji, huddles…). The gaps, built:

- **Live location** (`LOCATION` with `metadata.live { until, updatedAt, stopped? }`, `liveMinutes` 15 / 60 / 480 when sent;
  `POST /api/chat/messages/:id/live { lat, lng } | { stop: true }`, the sender only, at most a move every 10 s, 410 once
  over). The chat window watches the position while it's open and my live locations are running (`useNow`, not
  `Date.now()` while rendering). The location button opens `LocationSheet` (now or live). A web page can't move it in the
  background: the sheet says so.
- **Spoilers**: `||text||` in `RichText` (a covered button until tapped); `hideSpoilers` (`src/lib/spoilers.ts`) in list
  previews (`plainText`) and notifications.
- **Events with RSVP**: message type `EVENT` (`src/lib/chat-event.ts`: `newEvent`, `answer`, `eventIcs`), `POST
  /api/chat/messages/:id/rsvp { answer }` (the same answer again takes it back), the + menu and `/event`; the bubble has a
  date tile, the three answers, who said what, and Add to calendar (an .ics made in the browser).
- **QR codes** (the existing `ui/QrCode`) under a community's invite link and a new meeting's / My room's link.
- **Read receipts** (`users.readReceipts`, 0257; Settings → Privacy & security; `PATCH /users/me`, the fast path's
  `usersMe`): the messages route sends a member's `lastReadAt` only when both they and I keep receipts on.
- The jump-to-latest button moves above the hints bar (`hasHints`).
- **Left out on purpose:** phone dial-in, live streaming to YouTube (paid services), remote control of a shared screen
  (risky), GIF search (Tenor / Giphy need an account and key: [owner] if wanted).

## M345: recurring meetings, and "Join muted" and "Chat off" for hosts (19 Nov)

Meet & call's gaps from M344's inventory. The host already had: the waiting room, mute everyone, ask to unmute, stop
someone's video, co-hosts, spotlight, lower all hands, remove, end for everyone, polls, breakouts, webinar and Q&A.

- **Recurring meetings** (`src/lib/meeting-repeat.ts`: `repeatDates` daily / weekdays / weekly / biweekly / monthly, at
  most 10): `scheduleCall` (`src/server/scheduled-calls.ts`) takes `{ repeat, times }` and creates every date as its own
  scheduled call (and class-calendar event), within the 6 months ahead; one notification names the series. Cancelling one
  leaves the others (each is a row). About three queries a meeting, so ten stays under D1's 50 a request.
- **Host switches** (CallRoom in `cloudflare/worker.ts`): `control` actions `entry-muted` and `chat-off` (`on`), stored in
  the room's storage, broadcast as `room-setting`; `welcome` carries `settings`; a non-host joining while `entry-muted` is
  sent `control mute` with `entry: true` (their toast says why); the room's chat drops non-host lines while `chat-off`.
  `PeoplePanel` shows the two chips next to the waiting room's; `CallChatPanel locked` replaces the box with a note
  (the room's own chat only: a chat call's messages go to that chat).
- **Left out:** handing the host role to someone else (co-hosts cover it), phone dial-in and live streaming (paid),
  remote control (risky), touch-up and low-light filters (the effects pipeline would need a new pass).

## M346 (19 Nov): dark maps, and a smoother landing near the Earth

The owner, 19 Nov: "when i scroll towards here then it lags a lot… and the maps is not dark, any of the maps is not
dark"; then "the whole main page is laggy".
- **Maps:** every map already followed dark mode, but with Apple Maps' blue-slate land and bright navy sea, which read as
  a light panel on the near-black page. Now a night map: the canvas maps (`WorldCanvas` `PAL.dark`: Trace, Relief, Green,
  aid boxes) and the street maps (`map-style.ts` `DARK`: Travel, Green's places, Relief's alerts) have near-black land a
  shade above the page, ink-blue water, dim roads, lighter labels; Travel's 3D buildings are darker, and its sky
  (`skyFor`) is a night sky in dark mode whatever the hour (the daytime blue glowed over the dark globe).
- **The landing's lag** was on the graphics chip, not the page's code (a 4×-slowed phone and a computer kept up in
  `earth-scroll`-style checks). Four things, all lighter now: the app scene behind the page (`AppBackdrop`) rests while
  the page scrolls on a background thread too (it was still handing a full-screen picture over 30 times a second
  mid-scroll); the Earth (`EarthGlobe`) starts only once the scroll stops (`whenStill`: its picture goes to the chip in
  one go), draws at most 1.5 pixels a point, and takes the 4096 picture only past 1,300 pixels across; dark mode's
  clouds are their own dimmed picture (`/geo/clouds-dark.webp`, made by `scripts/assets/earth-pictures.py`) in place of
  a filter on the drifting layer; the five 64 px blur glows on the landing's cards are radial gradients.
- **Measured** (the built site, a phone at 4× slower CPU): slow frames near the Earth 12 → 7. The container has no real
  graphics chip, so what the owner saw (the chip's work) can't be measured here; ask the owner how it feels.
- **Rules for code that builds on it:** decorative canvases rest while `html[data-scrolling]`, on a thread too; no CSS
  `filter` on anything that moves (bake it into the picture); no big `blur()` glows (a radial gradient); a WebGL scene's
  first frame (textures, shaders) waits for the scroll to stop.
- **Left out:** the mask fading the Earth's lower edge (cheap: redrawn only with the Earth's 30 frames, not the scroll).

## M351 (20 Nov): whatever a press opens eases in, everywhere

The owner, 20 Nov: "make every other button when i click and when it try to open something then it should show smooth
animations"; then, of M350's "only the maps": "please do this every where in the project". The shared sheets and
dialogs already animated; the gaps were hand-made menus, drop-downs, pop-ups and sections on single screens (86 files).
So the motion layer does it (`scroll-motion.ts`, `opened`): within 0.8 s of a press (pointer, or Enter / Space), new
parts that appear on screen ease in, at most 6: a floating one (absolute / fixed: a menu, a drop-down) grows from the
press (`pressOrigin`, tested) 0.96 → 1 while it fades in; one in the page's flow (a section, a tab's content) fades in
rising 8 px. The transform is added (`composite: 'add'`), so a part's own centring stays. Skipped: anything already
moving (`moving`: its own CSS animation, framer-motion's inline styles, WAAPI), lists redrawn (over 12 new rows or
moved rows: morph() handles them), toasts, loading views, the page's frame, `[data-no-motion]`, a new page (its own
entrance), Reduce Motion. Checked: the top bar's UniVersity, Learn and More menus now open this way; the Language menu
keeps its own animation, not two.
- **Rule:** a new pop-up needs nothing to animate; give it its own CSS animation only for a different entrance (the
  layer then leaves it alone). Exits are each component's own (closing still removes most at once).

## M352 (20 Nov): rounder, iOS-smooth corners everywhere

The owner, 20 Nov: "make sure every area or sections and design is round and corners smooth like how apple ios does".
One block at the end of `globals.css`: every step of Tailwind's roundness one notch larger (`--radius-sm` 6 px … `--radius-3xl`
28 px; plain `rounded` 6 px) and cards from 12 px (M134's Ballast reels) to 18 px (`--radius-card`); where the browser
draws continuous corners (`@supports (corner-shape: squircle)`: Chrome now; Safari and Firefox keep the rounder plain
corners) the steps grow more (a squircle at the same radius looks tighter: cards 24 px, `rounded-xl` 22 px) and every
rounded part takes `corner-shape: squircle` (`[class*="rounded-"]`, the button, field, menu-row and segmented classes);
circles and pills (`…-full`) and `rounded-none` stay as they are. Radii only: nothing moves or resizes (checked: no
sideways scroll at 390 and 1280 on the student home, Settings and Trace).
- **Rule:** use Tailwind's `rounded-*` steps or `--radius-card` (they follow this block); a hard-coded radius won't.

## M356 (20 Nov): public transport in Directions

The owner, 20 Nov (Directions from Paris to Lyon): "why there are no public transport here?"; then "i need both and it
should show all the transport and options just like google and apple maps does".
- **Why no timetables of our own:** the routers we use (FOSSGIS / OSRM) know roads and paths only. Timetables come from
  paid services (an account and a charge per search: the owner's decision, **[owner]**, asked) or Transitous, whose
  rules allow only open-source, non-commercial apps under ~720 searches a day (transitous.org/api): UniVerse has paid
  plans and no open-source licence, so it isn't used.
- **What's there now:** a fourth way of travel, **Public transport**, beside car, walk and bike (`DirMode` in
  `MapTools.tsx`: no router request for it; `startNav` refuses it). It shows `TransitWays.tsx`: every way to get there,
  quickest first (`waysBetween` in `src/lib/transit-options.ts`, tested): bus, tram or metro close by; train and coach
  between towns; a flight once it's far; the drive to compare; each with a time and CO₂ estimated from the distance
  (`TRAVEL_FACTORS`, the same as the trip footprint) and where to see or book it (Rome2Rio, Google Flights; the drive
  switches to the car route). Then **Exact departures, lines and changes**: Google Maps, Apple Maps and Citymapper with
  the trip filled in (their documented links, `transitApps`), and Rome2Rio to compare with prices. The map frames both
  ends. The old "Public transport in Google Maps" link at the very bottom of the turns is gone (the tab replaces it).
- Checked in a browser (Paris → Lyon, place lookups stubbed: this container can't reach them): train ~2 h 20, flight
  ~3 h, drive ~6 h, coach ~7 h 25, with CO₂; the three apps' links; 1280 dark and 390 light, axe clean.
